name: application-goal-progress-card
title: Goal Progress Card
description: Target-vs-actual card with a pacing indicator and projected-finish note, driven by a typed current/target/pacing prop contract.
useWhen: Tracking a time-bound goal (revenue, signups, tasks) where progress should be compared against an expected pace, not just a raw percentage.
Users benefit from a projection ('on track to finish at X by date') rather than only the current value.
A dashboard needs a single-goal focus card distinct from a generic percent-complete progress bar.
avoidWhen: You only need to show a simple percent-complete value — use the plain progress-bars component instead.
The metric is a resource quota with a hard ceiling (e.g. storage limit) — use the Usage Meter Card instead, which is threshold-alerting rather than pacing-focused.
There is no time dimension or expected pace to compare against — a stat tile communicates a single value more simply.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a single fixed-width block with intrinsic sizing; place it in your own dashboard grid to control column count at each breakpoint.
accessibility: The pacing badge pairs a color dot with an explicit text label ('Ahead of pace', 'Behind pace'), not color alone.
The expected-pace marker on the progress track is a supplementary visual cue; the 'Expected today: X%' text below is the accessible source of truth.
The projection note is rendered as real paragraph text so screen readers announce the full projected outcome, not just a number.

variants.title: Goal Progress Card
variants.description: Goal card with current-vs-target value, a progress bar showing an expected-pace marker, percent labels, and a projected-finish note.
accessibility: The expected-pace tick mark on the bar is decorative; the numeric 'Expected today' label carries the actual meaning.

variants.title: Goal Progress Card (Dark)
variants.description: Goal-tracking card adapted for dark surfaces with the same pacing badge, progress bar, and projection-note structure.
accessibility: Pacing badge, progress fill, and projection text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
